inserted.question_text: What is the minimum substantive rank a civil servant must hold in the Directorate cadre to be eligible to apply for the post of Permanent Secretary in the Federal Civil Service?
According to the Public Service Rules (PSR), what is the minimum remaining active service requirement for a candidate applying for the post of Permanent Secretary?
What are the primary stages involved in the selection and promotion process for Permanent Secretaries in the Federal Civil Service?
Can a civil servant with a pending disciplinary case or active interdiction apply for the post of Permanent Secretary?
According to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, who is empowered to appoint a person to the office of Permanent Secretary in the Federal Civil Service?
In the context of the civil service, which of the following best describes the primary role of a Permanent Secretary?
What policy principle guides the appointment of Permanent Secretaries at the Federal level to ensure inclusivity and geographical spread?
In the promotion examination for the post of Permanent Secretary, which of the following is typically the main focus of the Policy and Administration paper?
Why is continuous participation in management and leadership courses (such as those from ASCON) highly regarded in the selection process for Permanent Secretaries?
Why has the ICT Assessment become a critical stage in the Permanent Secretary promotion examination?
Which body is primarily responsible for the final approval of conversion of officers on Grade Level 07 to 13 in the Federal Civil Service?
What is the fundamental distinction between "Reinstatement" and "Condonation of Service" under the Nigerian Public Service Rules (PSR)?
What is the specific role of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (HCSF) in processing an application for condonation of service for a senior officer?
What is the primary implication of condonation of service on a civil servant's retirement benefits?
What is the fundamental difference between the "Termination of Appointment" and "Dismissal" in the civil service?
An officer on a probationary appointment can have their appointment terminated by the Commission. What notice or remuneration is standard in lieu of notice?
If a permanent, pensionable officer's position is completely eliminated due to government restructuring, what is the appropriate term for their exit from service?
Which of the following is considered an act of "Serious Misconduct" that can lead directly to dismissal rather than a simple termination?
Who has the ultimate statutory authority to terminate or dismiss a civil servant on Grade Level 07 and above?
When an officer's appointment is terminated due to general inefficiency, what entitlement does the officer typically retain regarding retirement benefits, unlike a dismissed officer?
